sentences.text: Applicant has filed this second repeat bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

Applicant is in custody since 12/10/2022 in connection with Crime No.19/2022 registered at Police Station S.T.F., Indore, District Indore (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of IPC.

Brief facts of the case are that complainant Yaduvendra Mishra and Arjun Mishra had filed a complaint with the office of Special Task Force, Indore stating that they had paid certain amount to the applicant and other co-accused persons to get job in Military Engineering Service, Govt. of India,
Public Works Department, Environment Department, etc.
When they demanded back their money from the applicant and other co-accused, they refused to return the amount.
Accordingly, offence has been registered.

sentences.text: Applicant's first application preferred under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. has been dismissed on merit by this Court vide order dated 07/12/2022 passed in M.Cr.C.No.56533/2022.

Applicant has filed this second repeated bail application on the ground that after rejecting his earlier bail application, co-accused Narendra has been enlarged on bail by this Court v i d e order dated 19/01/2023 passed in M.Cr.C.No.57947/2022.
He has been made accused on the basis of memorandum under Section 27 of the Evidence Act given by the co-accused.
He is not having any criminal antecedent.
Hence, in the aforesaid change circumstances and on the ground of parity, he be released on bail.
Per-contra, learned counsel for respondent/ State opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection by submitting that earlier bail application o f present applicant was rejected on merit.
Thereafter, there is no material change in the circumstances.
Hence, applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.
Perused the impugned order of the trial Court, the statements of the witnesses as well as the case dairy.

This Court has carefully gone through the arguments advanced by both the parties, nature of allegation as also taking note of the fact that applicant's earlier application was rejected on merit while considering all the facts and circumstances of the case and also considering the fact that co-accused Sandeep and Devendra were enlarged on bail on the basis of compromise, which taken place between the complainant and other co-accused persons and the amount in question has been returned to the concerned victim persons.

Co- accused Narendra has also been enlarged on bail on the similar ground but in the instant case no compromise has taken place between the complainant and the applicant and the amount in question has also not been returned to the concerned victim person by the present applicant.
Therefore, his case cannot be considered similar with the case of other co-accused persons, who have been enlarged on bail.
Therefore, there is no material change in the circumstances in which the applicant can be enlarged on bail.
Hence, this second repeat bail application is hereby rejected.
Certified copy as per rules.
(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE Tej Arpit vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32576340/
